source.paper: Problem of the Week (labelled Volume 2, Set 12, Olympiad 3, 3D)

prompt: The clock shown below loses 12 minutes every hour. It shows the correct time now. **In how many hours will it next show the correct time?**

solutions.title: Count the minutes it must lose
solutions.body:
This is the official MOEMS strategy.

A 12-hour clock looks right again when it has fallen behind by exactly 12 hours. That is $12 \times 60 = 720$ minutes.

It loses 12 minutes each hour, so it needs $720 \div 12 = 60$ hours.

**Answer: 60 hours**

solutions.title: How far the clock's hands move
solutions.body:
In each real hour, the slow clock moves only $60 - 12 = 48$ minutes.

The clock shows the correct time again when the real time has gone around the dial exactly one more time than the slow clock. Every hour the slow clock falls 12 minutes further behind, and a whole trip around the dial is 12 hours = 720 minutes.

Check after 60 hours: real time moved $60$ hours $= 5$ full turns of 12 hours. The slow clock moved $60 \times 48 = 2880$ minutes $= 48$ hours $= 4$ full turns. Both hands point to the same place ✓

**Answer: 60 hours**
